events.text: Q1 FY26 print: sales +18% YoY to US$4.35B, EPS +30% to US$0.70 (both at the top of the guide); op margin +220bp to 20.2%; GM 39.1%; ROIC 13.5%; FCF US$188M. Optical US$1.8B (+36% YoY), net income +93% YoY. 8th consecutive quarter of YoY sales growth.

On the up-to-US$6B agreement with Meta, Corning concluded two more hyperscaler LTAs of similar size/duration and is working on others. Carrier had its best quarter in years in FTTH + DCI; the Lumen agreement was expanded/extended.

Q2 2026 guide: sales ~US$4.6B (+14% YoY), EPS US$0.73–0.77 (+25%), absorbing ~US$0.07 of solar-wafer drag. FY CapEx ~US$1.7B. Springboard: vs the Q4 2023 base, +33% sales / +79% EPS / +390bp op margin; the plan was raised to +US$11B of annualized sales by 2028, to be extended to 2030 at the May 6 event.

events.src: GLW · Q1 FY26 Q&A (Weeks, w/ Wamsi Mohan/BofA)
events.text: Weeks: would let optical ROIC exceed the glass businesses, and gross/profit margins could "eclipse" Display. Hyperscaler/Nvidia LTAs use prepayments + take-or-pay to de-risk capex, so Corning grows in AI without a cash-flow dip.

MS (Meta Marshall) ranks GLW #2 in the optical basket behind Lumentum on "control of its own destiny"; the May 6 day "certainly exceeded" reduced expectations. Post-Nvidia GLW trades ~30x CY2028 vs ~25x Lumentum/Coherent — a premium to the optical pack. Would be "more aggressive buyers on down days". Order: Lumentum > Corning > Coherent > Ciena.

Lumentum's CEO characterized the NVDA-Corning deal as a large purchase agreement similar in structure to LITE's laser deal but without the ~US$2B equity backend — reads Jensen "buying fibers" as a sign NVDA is preparing to "own the wiring of scale-up clusters", more fiber in the racks and a shift from copper/Amphenol connectors to glass inside the rack.

The Nvidia partnership (announced before May 6) adds a multibillion-dollar upfront prepayment, a ~US$3.2B warrant for Nvidia to take equity, 10x US connectivity capacity, +50% fiber, and anchors the US$10B Photonics build. The DCI target of "US$1B medium term" looked conservative to some vs the US$1B Arista already has.
GLW present at JPM's TMT conference (2026-05-19); buyback cadence ongoing.

JPM moved to Neutral, PT US$185, framed around the Photonics TAM and ~US$8 of 2030E EPS, noting an Amazon deal is already "baked in Springboard" — the shift in stance reflects valuation/expectations catching up to the post-May 6 high, not a demand call.

MS's live read hours after the Q2 print hit the tape — "probably the biggest piece of news kind of this morning is just the Corning print" (Equal-weight / PT $180 unchanged). On the quarter: "optical results were generally within expectations. We did see re-acceleration of the enterprise business to 65% year-over-year growth, but the telco business was kind of essentially flat. So a little bit of a surprise. We'll see if they were just reallocating some of their supply there" — note the basis gap with the print/Barclays, which have Carrier DOWN 9% q/q, and the different cause she offers (supply reallocation to Enterprise vs 1Q pull-ins / LTA lumpiness). On the guide, the most precise version of the "what did the Street actually want" question: "the guide did not show a tremendous amount of upside… a little bit light from both a revenue and an EPS standpoint. So certainly not pointing to probably the couple of cents of upside that they would have needed to post on EPS and I think we were forecasting about 200 million of upside that they could have posted on the revenue side." Her interpretation is the two-sided part, and the least damaging of the four diagnoses on the print: "just kind of showing the sold-out conditions within optical, and just that these valuations had definitely rerated from historical levels. So really what we're doing now is contracting more towards historical valuations, but still on much more elevated EPS" — a capacity constraint, not a demand problem, with the drawdown as multiple normalisation onto a structurally higher earnings base. Broader optical bias turned "maybe a little bit more cautious, just because of concerns around CPO timing… we don't lean on there being delays… but just the amount of scale that we think that it will have is just a little bit lower in 2028 versus where expectations had been. That's created a little bit of a breather on the space in general" — the calendar is unchanged, the 2028 penetration rate comes down.
